proposedQuestion.subject: physics
proposedQuestion.topic: Optimal pulling angle with kinetic friction
proposedQuestion.prompt: At a given instant a 5 kg crate is sliding RIGHT across a horizontal floor. A20 N force is directed to the right at adjustable angle theta in[0°,90°] above horizontal. With mu_k=0.5 and g=10 m/s², which angle maximizes its SIGNED horizontal acceleration (right positive) at that instant? The crate remains in contact.
proposedQuestion.explanation: N=50-20sin(theta)>0 throughout the allowed domain. While sliding right, friction is left and a=4[cos(theta)+0.5sin(theta)]-5. Cauchy-Schwarz gives cos(theta)+0.5sin(theta)<=sqrt(1.25), with equality at tan(theta)=0.5. Thus the maximum signed acceleration occurs at arctan(0.5); it is sqrt(20)-5≈-0.528 m/s², still a deceleration. The question does not claim the crate accelerates rightward.

proposedQuestion.topic: Pendulum, accelerating lift, kinetic floor friction and system balance
proposedQuestion.prompt: An 8 kg cart slides RIGHT on the horizontal floor of a lift accelerating upward at2 m/s². A2 kg bob hangs from the cart and remains at rest relative to it, with its string37° from vertical. A horizontal motor force F drives the cart; kinetic friction between cart and lift floor has coefficient0.1. Take g=10 m/s²,sin37°=0.6,cos37°=0.8; neglect all other horizontal forces. Find the pair (F,string tension).
proposedQuestion.explanation: Effective vertical gravity is12 m/s² in the lift. Bob vertical balance gives Tcos37=2(12), so T=30 N. Horizontal bob balance gives ax=Tsin37/2=9 m/s². Floor normal on the cart is its own effective weight8(12) plus the bob downward string component Tcos37=24, so N=120 N and kinetic friction12 N left. The cart+bob system has total horizontal mass10 kg: F-12=10(9), hence F=102 N. Separate cart FBD F-12-18=8(9) confirms the result.
